sonnet.problem: The joke is about the word 'Behold' at the start of God's quoted words. That makes the way Scripture is written the joke.
sonnet.rule: Holy things, like the ark, and the way Scripture is written are never the joke.

sonnet.problem: The question says 'God took their fathers' but never says whose fathers. The baker can't see the earlier card, so 'their' has no clear antecedent.
sonnet.rule: The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

sonnet.problem: The card is a bare quote, 'I disregarded them,' with no voice and no context. The baker isn't told who 'them' is, so the moment doesn't make sense on its own.
sonnet.rule: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

sonnet.problem: The card says 'No more reminders,' which the text doesn't say. Verse 11 is about no longer teaching a neighbor or brother to 'Know the Lord.' This is narration, not a joke, so it stretches the text.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: The question asks the baker to complete the end of a line, 'remember their sins ___,' with wording they haven't seen. The story card quoted only the first half of the verse.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

sonnet.problem: The joke refers to 'a shiny new stamper showing up on the counter' without saying what it is or that it replaced him. A baker who doesn't know his backstory won't get it.
sonnet.rule: Bakers may not know anything about his story. Anything from his backstory, like the drawer, the Millers, the shiny new stamper or the angel, is said in the line itself
